name: A machine-level benchmark CSV labels its Mac Studio test rig 'M4 Ultra (192 GB)' with the M3 Ultra's exact specs, producing an accelerator record for a part whose only evidence is the benchmark label
symptom: data/accelerators/apple-m4-ultra.json claims 192 GB unified at 819 GB/s, sourced only to a benchmark CSV. apple-m3-ultra already holds the identical bandwidth (819 GB/s) sourced to Apple's own spec sheet. An M4 Max is 546 GB/s, so a fused 'M4 Ultra' would not land on 819 GB/s; 819 GB/s at 192 GB is the M3 Ultra configuration.
root_cause: Machine-level benchmark exports name their test rig in a free-text column. The siliconscore CSV files the Mac Studio it measured as 'M4 Ultra (192 GB)'. The 16 benchmark records that cite this accelerator are real tok/s measurements - only the machine attribution is unsupported.
workaround: Attribute Mac Studio measurements to apple-m3-ultra unless a record cites an Apple spec sheet for the part. Do not add an M4 Ultra to a price or fit ranking on CSV evidence alone.
notes: No Apple specification document for an M4 Ultra was located; the only citation is the benchmark CSV. Kept as a record rather than deleted because 16 benchmark records reference the accelerator id, and a silent delete would orphan them. Benchmarks each carry their own measured figures and remain usable.
